title: Defensive Patterns against Tool‑Selection and LLM‑as‑Judge Prompt‑Injection in Weakly‑Constrained NetOps Agents (Repaired Preregistration)
research_question: Which defensive architecture pattern (constrained tool-surface + independent verifier + authenticated tool‑handoff) most reliably reduces successful tool‑selection and LLM‑as‑judge prompt‑injection attacks relative to an unconstrained baseline in weakly‑constrained NetOps agent workflows?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (primary, confirmatory, paired): The constrained+independent-verifier+authenticated-handoff defense reduces attacker success rate by ≥50% (relative reduction) versus the unconstrained baseline when tested on the same attack attempts (paired design).

H2 (confirmatory, paired): The operational false‑positive rate on benign tasks introduced by the constrained+verifier+handoff defense remains <10% compared to baseline (measured as proportion of benign tasks flagged/blocked).
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How do the constrained-only and independent-verifier-only patterns compare to the combined pattern in absolute attacker success rate and latency?
EQ2: How robust is the combined defense under an adaptive adversary that iteratively probes verifier behavior (preregistered adaptive follow-up)?
EQ3: Which automatic verifier heuristics (syntactic tool-call whitelist, semantic matcher, signature verification) contribute most to reduced attack success (ablation)?
benchmark_scope: Public synthetic NetOps emulation suite (synthetic_paired_llm_benchmark_v1 adapter–compatible task set).
Emulated multi-vendor device models limited to safe, read-only and dry-run configuration templates (no destructive outputs).
Attack corpus published alongside code (public repository) and limited to the supplied simulated tool descriptions and prompt families.
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (attack success rate difference computed on paired attack attempts: baseline run vs defended run on same attack input)
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired sample: N_pairs = 500 distinct attack attempts. Each attack attempt executed twice (paired): once under unconstrained baseline agent and once under constrained+verifier+authenticated-handoff defense, using identical attack input and RNG seeds where available. Benign-safety sample: 500 benign tasks executed under same paired regime. All RNG seeds, prompt-selection seeds, and sampled indices will be published. Total planned agent runs = 2000; planned average model calls/run = 3.0; planned total model calls estimate = 6000 (within manifest limit).
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: ≥50% relative reduction (example: baseline 30% → defended 15%, absolute diff 0.15). Simulation-based paired-binomial power assessment assuming baseline p0=0.30, defended p1=0.15, α=0.05, target power=0.80; with 500 pairs simulation yields ≥0.80 power. Sensitivity analyses: recompute under p0=0.20 and p0=0.40 and under varying within-pair concordance; seeds published.
exclusion_rules: Exclude pair when provider/API or infrastructure error occurs in either paired run (deterministic exclusion per missingness_plan).
Exclude benign task run when canonicalization or signature verification fails (counted as false-positive event and logged).
missingness_plan: If an agent run fails due to infrastructure/provider API failure, apply analysis executor's failed_call_treatment: primary treatment = complete_pair_primary (exclude entire pair). Sensitivity analysis: complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity (treat missing run as attack success=0). All technical failures, retries, causes, timestamps, and hashes will be logged and published. No manual adjudication; deterministic rules govern inclusion/exclusion.
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory analysis executed by paired_binary_analysis_v1. For each attack pair record baseline_success ∈ {0,1} and defended_success ∈ {0,1}. Compute paired success-rate difference (defended minus baseline) with 95% CI via exact paired/binomial methods implemented by paired_binary_analysis_v1. Primary decision rule: declare H1 supported if observed relative reduction ≥50% AND 95% CI lower bound excludes reductions <50% under preregistered baseline assumption. H2 assessed with a one-sided test (false-positive rate <10%) using exact binomial methods. Secondary analyses (absolute rates, ablations, latency) are exploratory and reported without confirmatory p-values.
multiplicity_plan: Two primary confirmatory estimands: H1 (paired success-rate reduction) and H2 (benign false-positive <10%). Both reported explicitly as primary. All additional comparisons (constrained-only, verifier-only, ablations, adaptive follow-ups) are exploratory and will not receive alpha correction; multiplicity statement will be included in manuscript.
contamination_plan: Benchmark: synthetic_paired_llm_benchmark_v1. Risk factors: possible overlap between attack corpus and closed-model training data (cannot be excluded); task-sampling contamination mitigated by deterministic pairing and published seeds; adaptive adversary learning across runs mitigated by isolated paired execution and preregistered adaptive-followup design. Detection: automated hash-based provenance checks for inputs and responses; flagging rules for provider errors and canonicalization/signature failures. Analysis treatment: technical-failure pairs excluded under primary analysis; sensitivity analyses include worst-case treatments. Residual uncertainty documented in manuscript.
stopping_rule: Stop when all preregistered paired executions complete (500 attack pairs + 500 benign pairs) OR when the planned model-call budget (maximum_model_calls = 6000) is exhausted OR when wall-clock execution reaches the capability manifest limit (maximum_wall_clock_days = 7). Any early stop and reason will be logged and published.
planned_outputs: IEEE-format short paper (≤5 pages) with mandatory Disclosure Statement
Public repository with code, attack corpus, canonicalizer, verifier rules, signed artifact hashes, raw model responses, and analysis notebooks
